properties.statement:
REPORTED BY ALEX (who:alex) 2026-08-29 from `art:grok-shell-feedback-2026-08-29` — grok-shell-reflow2 1.0.13, reflow2 0.42.0, macOS. Two refusals, both cross-type:

    add_requirement  -> refused, naming an existing ChangeEvent
    add_decision     -> refused, naming an existing Capability

Both were resolved with `distinct_from` naming the other-typed node, after which the create succeeded. ⭐ HE IS EXPLICIT THAT THE REFUSAL TEXT IS GOOD: *"clear and actionable."* This is not a complaint about the message, and the guard is not misfiring in the sense of matching unrelated text — the nodes it named really did say the same thing in the same words.

🛑 THE DEFECT IS THAT THE GUARD CANNOT TELL A SECOND LAYER FROM A SECOND COPY, AND THE DESIGN'S OWN PRESCRIBED WORKFLOW PRODUCES THE FIRST. reflow2 instructs a session to record what shipped as a ChangeEvent AND what must stay true as a Requirement AND why it was chosen as a Decision. Those are deliberately different records of one idea, at different layers, and the served instructions ask for all of them. So an agent following the loop HONESTLY — change event first, then the durable intent — trips the guard every time, in his words: *"`distinct_from` works; it is just the default path now."*

WHAT IT COSTS: one refused round-trip per honest capture, and a standing invitation to skip the second record rather than argue with the tool. The second failure mode is the expensive one and it is INVISIBLE — a Requirement never written because the guard made it awkward leaves no trace anywhere, and `intent 73%` is already this design's weakest axis.

⚠️ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and it decides the repair:

① **Cross-type matching is not simply wrong.** "You already have a Capability that says this" is a genuinely useful catch, and same-type-only matching would lose it. Nobody has counted how often a cross-type hit is a real duplicate versus the layered-capture case, and without that number a change here is a guess.

② **The two directions may not be symmetric.** ChangeEvent -> Requirement is the prescribed loop and is ALWAYS legitimate. Capability -> Decision (his second case) is less clearly so — a Decision restating a Capability may be a real duplicate. Treating all cross-type pairs alike would over-correct on the strength of the first case.

③ **The type pair is already known at the call site**, so a narrower answer than on/off exists and has not been costed: keep the refusal but change what it SAYS when the near-match is a different type — name the layer relationship (*"this looks like the ChangeEvent for the same work; if this is the durable requirement behind it, pass distinct_from"*) rather than presenting it as a duplicate. That would keep every real catch and remove the friction, and it is a message change rather than a behaviour change.

📌 NOT A REGRESSION: the guard has behaved this way since `chg:search-first-fires-at-the-tool` (v0.28.0), which normalises the threshold against the new node's own in-query score and searches the design without restricting by type. This is the first report of the consequence — twelve days after the same reporter's first report, and from the only seat known to be running the loop end-to-end by hand.

═══ RECURRENCE #3, dev_storyflow 2026-09-06 on 0.48.0 (triaged 2026-09-07) ═══ "The near-duplicate guard fires on the promotion itself, every time — promoting a brainstorm option into a Requirement is, by construction, a node that says something close to the Decision it came from — and the guard refused all FOUR promotions until re-sent with distinct_from. Same for the capability that answers a verification's finding (refused against the verification). Eight extra round-trips for the one relationship the skill tells you to create." Wish #33: accept when the near-match is the node the caller is about to relate, or `evolves_from` on add_requirement. STATE OF THE PAIRS: (Requirement, Decision) — the promotion — IS a prescribed layer pair since 0.49.0 (#433), so four of the eight refusals do not happen on a current build; (Capability, Verification) — the check that found the need beside the capability that answers it — is NOT in PRESCRIBED_LAYER_PAIRS and is the new instance of this class. The reporter's `evolves_from` suggestion is a stronger discriminator than the type pair: the caller names the very node the guard will match, and the edge it is about to draw is the proof it is a layer, not a copy. Counted; the pair addition is a one-line fix and `evolves_from` a design question.
